**FCA welcomes UKPI launch as open banking scheme goes live**

*The UK Payments Initiative has formally launched its account-to-account payments scheme, with FCA endorsement and participation from major banks and fintechs, moving variable recurring payments from pilot to commercial reality.*

UKPI, the industry body formed to commercialise open banking payments in the UK, went live on June 2 with a scheme enabling recurring and automated account-to-account payments via commercial variable recurring payments. The FCA issued a statement welcoming the launch and confirming it aligns with the regulator's broader open banking and open finance roadmap.

The scheme has secured backing from the UK's largest banks and a roster of fintechs, positioning it as a direct alternative to card network rails for subscription and utility payments. UKPI has framed the launch as a step toward reducing merchant dependence on Visa and Mastercard for recurring billing, a goal that has been discussed for years but lacked a coordinated commercial vehicle.

The FCA noted it plans to consult on a long-term regulatory framework for open banking by the end of 2026, contingent on forthcoming legislative powers. That timeline matters: UKPI's commercial momentum will depend on whether regulatory certainty arrives fast enough to sustain bank and fintech commitment beyond the initial launch.

*Sources: [Open banking takes next step forward with launch of UK Payments Initiative scheme](https://www.fca.org.uk/news/statements/open-banking-launch-uk-payments-initiative-scheme) — FCA | [UK Payments Initiative launches to challenge Visa and Mastercard stranglehold](https://www.finextra.com/newsarticle/47842/uk-payments-initiative-launches-to-challenge-visa-and-mastercard-stranglehold) — Finextra | [UK Payments Initiative launches new A2A payments scheme in 'defining moment'](https://www.openbankingexpo.com/news/uk-payments-initiative-launches-new-a2a-payments-scheme-in-defining-moment/) — Open Banking Expo | [UK payments initiative launches open banking recurring payments scheme](https://tradersunion.com/news/regulators/show/2205112-uk-open-banking-recurring-payments/) — Traders Union*

**ING, Worldline and Mastercard complete Europe's first agentic payment**

*A live end-to-end agentic payment transaction in Europe signals that AI-initiated commerce is moving from concept to operational reality, with card network and bank infrastructure already in place to support it.*

ING, Worldline and Mastercard have executed what they describe as Europe's first end-to-end agentic payment transaction. The transaction was completed live, with an AI agent initiating and completing a payment on behalf of a user through existing payment infrastructure, rather than requiring manual intervention at the authorisation stage.

Agentic payments — where AI systems act autonomously to make purchases or settle obligations — have been a talking point since the emergence of commercial AI agents in 2025. This transaction demonstrates that the plumbing to support them already exists within current card and banking rails, rather than requiring entirely new infrastructure. The involvement of a major bank, a large processor and a card network gives the proof point more weight than a startup demo.

The practical question remains how quickly consumer trust and regulatory comfort will catch up with the technical capability. Authentication, liability and consent frameworks for AI-initiated payments are largely unaddressed in current European regulation. But the fact that established players are now executing live transactions, rather than publishing white papers, compresses the timeline for those conversations.

*Sources: [Worldline, ING, and Mastercard execute first European agentic payment](https://thepaypers.com/payments/news/worldline-ing-and-mastercard-execute-first-european-agentic-payment) — The Paypers | [ING completes live end-to-end European agentic payment transaction](https://www.finextra.com/newsarticle/47844/ing-completes-live-end-to-end-european-agentic-payment-transaction) — Finextra*

**Chile's financial regulator amends open finance rules with new technical annex**

*Chile's CMF has updated its open finance regulation with a detailed technical annex, advancing one of Latin America's most structured approaches to data sharing in financial services.*

The Chilean Financial Market Commission (CMF) issued an amendment to General Rule No. 514 on June 1, updating the regulatory framework for the country's Open Finance System under the Fintech Law. The amendment incorporates a technical annex specifying implementation details for participants in the system.

Chile's approach is notable for its level of regulatory prescription compared with other Latin American markets. While Brazil has built open finance through central bank-led mandates and Mexico has moved more slowly under its own fintech law, Chile's CMF has opted for detailed rule-making that leaves less to industry interpretation. The addition of a technical annex suggests the regulator is moving toward operational readiness rather than still debating principles.

For European observers, Chile's progress is relevant as a comparator for how open finance frameworks develop outside the EU and UK. The CMF's willingness to iterate on its rules — amending rather than waiting for a comprehensive rewrite — offers a contrast to the EU's slower legislative cycle around PSD3 and the Financial Data Access regulation.

*Sources: [CMF amends regulation on Open Finance System, incorporates Technical Annex](https://www.cmfchile.cl/portal/principal/613/w3-article-110883.html) — CMF Chile*

**XFolio AI acquires Absolute Payment Solutions to build UK corporate treasury platform**

*A Paris-based treasury technology firm has acquired one of the UK's Pay.UK-accredited Bacs providers, combining payment processing with cash management in a single platform for mid-market corporates.*

XFolio AI has acquired Absolute Payment Solutions, a Pay.UK-accredited Bacs service provider, to create an integrated treasury and payments platform for UK corporates. The combined offering spans Bacs processing, open banking connectivity, risk management and cash management.

The deal is a small example of a broader pattern: treasury and payments functions converging into unified platforms, driven by corporate demand for fewer systems and better cash visibility. Absolute Payment Solutions' accreditation as a Bacs service provider — a relatively scarce licence — gives XFolio direct access to UK payment rails rather than relying on intermediaries.

XFolio AI is Paris-based, making this a cross-border acquisition that brings a European treasury technology firm into the UK payments infrastructure layer. For the UK mid-market, the proposition is straightforward: one platform where payments execution and treasury oversight sit together. Whether XFolio can compete effectively against established UK treasury management providers will depend on execution, but the acquisition of a licensed payments provider is a credible entry point.

*Sources: [XFolio AI Acquires Absolute Payment Solutions to Unify Treasury and Payments for UK Corporates](https://www.businesswire.com/news/home/20260602312059/en/XFolio-AI-Acquires-Absolute-Payment-Solutions-to-Unify-Treasury-and-Payments-for-UK-Corporates) — BusinessWire | [XFolio AI buys Absolute Payments to unify treasury and payments for UK corporates](https://www.finextra.com/pressarticle/110002/xfolio-ai-buys-absolute-payments-to-unify-treasury-and-payments-for-uk-corporates) — Finextra*
